finding.title: Split the 5 hand-written Dart files in this batch that exceed the 400-line AG-3 cap
finding.rule: AG-3 (hand-written Dart files stay under 400 lines)
finding.why: Files past the 400-line ratchet exceed per-file agent read budgets (content past the window is invisible to an agent editing it) and become dumping grounds -- completion_writer_test.dart in particular has absorbed unrelated tutoring-feature test content (see the triplicate-test finding) rather than staying scoped to CompletionWriter.
finding.recommendation: Split learning_screen.dart's private widgets (_StreakHeroCard, _LearnTaskCard, _BrowseSection, _CurriculumBrowseCard) into separate widget files; split completion_writer_test.dart and the two large repository test files along their existing numbered/grouped sections into per-concern files.
acceptance_criteria: find lib test -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400' no longer lists these 5 files

finding.title: Replace wall-clock DateTime.now() with fixed UTC literals in learning-repository test fixtures
finding.why: These three files read the real system clock (not even .toUtc()) to satisfy required timestamp columns, while sibling files in the same batch (completion_repository_curriculum_dedup_test.dart, completion_writer_test.dart, learning_ledger_repository_impl_test.dart) consistently use DateTime.now().toUtc() or fixed DateTime.utc(...) literals -- an inconsistent idiom that Rule 0's own check 6/15 ('No DateTime.now() outside core/time') explicitly cannot catch because it scopes only to lib/ and excludes test/ entirely.
finding.recommendation: Replace the bare DateTime.now() calls with fixed DateTime.utc(...) literals for these non-asserted fixture columns, matching the pattern already used elsewhere in the same batch.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn 'DateTime\.now()' test/features/learning --include='*.dart' returns no hits outside intentionally wall-clock-dependent assertions

evidence.quote:

finding.why: learning_screen_test.dart overrides dashboardActiveCurriculaProvider and dashboardUserModeProvider (lines 19-27) — I grepped learning_screen.dart's ref.watch calls and confirmed it reads neither provider; both overrides are dead, left over from before the screen was refactored onto dashboardActiveCurriculaStreamProvider/coarse-track providers. Its 'renders without error' and 'shows key UI elements' tests are a strict, weaker subset of learning_screen_l1_test.dart's empty-state tests (same setup, same assertion, less specific). Only the AppErrorView regression test (lines 70-93) is unique, and it doesn't exercise LearningScreen at all. Net effect: a second file that must be kept in sync with LearningScreen's provider surface for zero incremental protection, and it's currently out of sync (see the DB-leak finding above, which independently proves this).
finding.recommendation: Move the unique AppErrorView regression test to a location that actually reflects what it tests (e.g. a core/widgets AppErrorView test, or leave in learning_screen_test.dart renamed), delete the two redundant/stale tests and dead overrides, and remove learning_screen_test.dart per TQ-7 with the reason stated in the commit message.
acceptance_criteria: learning_screen_test.dart is deleted or contains only the non-duplicate AppErrorView test
No override in the remaining file references a provider LearningScreen does not read (grep ref.watch in learning_screen.dart against the override list)
